description: A composite figure combining three pseudo-3D EBSD stereographic blocks with six TEM bright-field (BF) images, all from the present low-density triplex steel after tensile straining. Top row: (a) an IPF map drawn as a 3D block oriented by RD, TD and ND axes, with a two-part colour key (hexagonal 0001/12-10/001 and cubic 0110/1-01/111) and a 50 µm scale bar; (a1) a phase map whose key assigns blue = γ, red = α and yellow = TiB2, showing elongated red α and yellow TiB2 bands aligned along one direction inside a blue γ matrix, 50 µm; (a2) a KAM map with a low-to-high colour bar, 50 µm. Middle row: (b–b2) BF TEM of the BCC (δ-ferrite) phase, each with a 200 nm scale bar — (b) a δ-ferrite grain distant from TiB2 with a BCC <110> SADP inset; (b1) dense dislocation pile-ups and tangles at a δ-ferrite/TiB2 interface (TiB2 marked in yellow, BCC <110> inset); (b2) a δ-ferrite region with a red diffraction inset labelled g = 011. Bottom row: (c–c2) BF TEM of the FCC (austenite) phase, 200 nm scale bars — (c) austenite away from TiB2 with an FCC <001> SADP inset; (c1) pile-ups with sparse tangles at an austenite/TiB2 interface (FCC <011> inset); (c2) an FCC region with a yellow inset labelled g = 1-11. Together the panels show that δ-ferrite carries much denser dislocation tangles than austenite, supporting the austenite-controlled ductility argument.

observations.observation: (a) is a 3D IPF block with RD, TD and ND reference axes and a two-part colour key containing the labels 0001, 12-10, 001, 0110, 1-01 and 111.
The (a1) phase-map colour key explicitly assigns blue = γ, red = α and yellow = TiB2.
In (a1) the red α and yellow TiB2 regions form elongated bands aligned along a single direction within the blue γ matrix.
(a2) is a KAM map whose colour bar is labelled only 'low' and 'high', so no numerical misorientation values are obtainable from it.
All three EBSD blocks (a, a1, a2) carry a 50 µm scale bar; all six TEM panels (b–b2, c–c2) carry a 200 nm scale bar.
The δ-ferrite TEM panels are labelled BCC and their SADP insets are indexed as BCC <110> in (b) and (b1), while (b2) shows an inset labelled g = 011.
The austenite TEM panels are labelled FCC and their SADP insets are indexed FCC <001> in (c) and FCC <011> in (c1), while (c2) shows an inset labelled g = 1-11.
The caption states that (b) is a δ-ferrite grain distant from TiB particles and (b1) shows dislocation pile-ups and tangles at a δ-ferrite/TiB interface.
The caption states that (c) is an austenite grain away from TiB particles and (c1) shows dislocation pile-ups with sparse tangles at the austenite/TiB interface.

The caption calls (b2) and (c2) the 'corresponding SADP' of the interface regions in (b1) and (c1), whereas in the pixels these panels are bright-field TEM images whose insets display the diffraction pattern and g vector; the two readings disagree.
The caption states that colour keys are provided in (a–a2) for the IPF maps, phase maps and KAM maps, respectively.

The citing text states that the good ductility of the present steel is primarily influenced by the introduction of austenite and its dislocation activities shown in Fig. 7, leading to dislocation hardening and enhanced deformation capability before damage initiation.

The citing text states that the harder δ-ferrite regions with higher dislocation densities increase the overall yield strength through a composite effect and remain an almost constant ~170 MPa contribution (>30 % of overall yield strength).

subfigures.description: Pseudo-3D stereographic IPF map (3D block) with RD, TD and ND axes marked and a two-part inverse-pole-figure colour key (0001, 12-10, 001 for the hexagonal set; 0110, 1-01, 111 for the cubic set); 50 µm scale bar.
Pseudo-3D phase map; colour key assigns blue = γ, red = α and yellow = TiB2. Elongated red α and yellow TiB2 bands run parallel to one direction through a blue γ matrix; 50 µm scale bar.
Pseudo-3D KAM (kernel average misorientation) map with a colour bar labelled only 'low' at one end and 'high' at the other; 50 µm scale bar. No numeric KAM values are printed.
Bright-field TEM of a δ-ferrite (labelled BCC) grain distant from TiB2 particles, with an SADP inset labelled BCC <110>; 200 nm scale bar.

Bright-field TEM showing dense dislocation pile-ups and tangles; the BCC label marks δ-ferrite and a yellow marker/TiB2 annotation marks the TiB2 region at the interface; SADP inset labelled BCC <110>; 200 nm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of a δ-ferrite (BCC) region with a red diffraction inset in which the reflection is labelled g = 011; 200 nm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of an austenite (labelled FCC) grain away from TiB2 particles, with an SADP inset labelled FCC <001>; 200 nm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM showing dislocation pile-ups with sparse tangles at an austenite/TiB2 interface; the FCC label marks austenite; SADP inset labelled FCC <011>; 200 nm scale bar.
Bright-field TEM of an FCC (austenite) region with a yellow diffraction inset in which the reflection is labelled g = 1-11; 200 nm scale bar.
